The brief

A shop floor,
translated to the web.

“Products that can’t be ordered online still get a call button and an email button — no dead ends.”

The shop was built in PrestaShop 1.7 for tools, machine parts and agricultural and industrial equipment. The theme was heavily customised through HTML, CSS and JavaScript, and products that cannot be ordered online get two buttons: one to call and one to request details by email. The contact form was rebuilt by editing TPL, HTML and CSS around Contact Form 7.

Products were imported by CSV from the previous WordPress site, and the shop stays permanently connected to the eMAG marketplace through an API feed module.

Build notes

What was actually built.

Four pieces of work that turned a standard PrestaShop install into a store that matches the way the business sells.

Four interventions
01 / Theme

A theme rebuilt by hand

HTML, CSS and JavaScript layered over PrestaShop templates to give the shop its own structure, product rhythm and a visual language built around red, black and machinery.

HTMLCSSJSTPL
02 / Products

Two ways to ask

Not every part belongs in a cart. Products that cannot be ordered online get a direct call button and an email request button, so the catalogue never becomes a dead end.

Product UXPHPTPL
03 / Contact

A form that fits the shop

The contact form was rebuilt by editing TPL, HTML and CSS around Contact Form 7 — same visual language as the rest of the store, no plugin default styling left behind.

Contact Form 7CSSTPL
04 / Catalogue

Imported, then connected

The catalogue was migrated by CSV from the old WordPress site, then connected to the eMAG marketplace with an API feed that keeps listings in sync.

CSVeMAG APICron
